slides.title:
The drinks retrace
somebody's travels.
slides.body:
Charles H. Baker Jr. was an American journalist who set out in 1931 to collect food and drink from places like Cairo, Calcutta, Buenos Aires and Yokohama. He wrote it up in 'The Gentleman's Companion' in 1939, and later in Esquire, Town & Country and a 1940s Gourmet column called 'Here's How'.

The World's 50 Best describes the bar as an opulent jewel that pays tribute to him "through a line-up of drinks that retrace his history of globetrotting". So the list is built as a route rather than a set of house styles — and Seoul gets folded into it. The Velvet Martini is listed with vermouth, fino sherry and Jeju hallabong citrus.

items.d: The martini runs vermouth, fino sherry and Jeju hallabong; the Coconut Grove adds Thai red curry and a fire tincture to rum and pineapple. 50 Best Discovery puts the average cocktail near US$23

caption:
A bar whose drinks list is really a travel route.

Charles H. sits on the lower level of the Four Seasons Hotel Seoul in Jongno-gu, and took No. 87 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2026. It is named for Charles H. Baker Jr., who collected drinks abroad from 1931 and published them in 1939 — the martini here carries Jeju hallabong.

Hours and phone differ between listings, so confirm first.

Sources in the last slide. Save it for your next trip.
